keyframe_review.note: New keyframe, 190-208; Cliopatria has no row and its Han shape (han-dynasty_184, 197, 207) keeps Jing Province inside the Han until 207, when ea-02-c's shape drops it. The Liu Biao page: Jing Province 'covering present-day Hubei and Hunan'. The Han province had seven commanderies (Nanyang, Nan, Jiangxia, Changsha, Guiyang, Wuling, Lingling, Jing Province page); Nanyang, the south-west of Henan, is left out because Wancheng was Zhang Xiu's (End of the Han page: he surrendered it to Cao Cao in 197) and no page says Liu Biao held it. No infobox area on the pages.

region.text: Jing Province under Liu Biao, 'covering present-day Hubei and Hunan'

ledger.note: 190: Liu Biao takes Jing Province. 'in 190 CE, when Dong Zhuo appointed him to the position after the death of its previous governor' (Inspector 190-192, Governor 192-208 in the infobox); the End of the Han page lists him as the man 'who controlled Jing Province' in 191.

region.text: Jing Province under Liu Biao, 'covering present-day Hubei and Hunan'

ledger.note: 208: Liu Biao dies and Jing Province is surrendered. 'Shortly after Cao Cao's main army began its offensive, Liu Biao died of illness' (8th month of Jian'an 13, 29 Aug to 27 Sep 208); his younger son Liu Cong 'chose to surrender instead of resisting' and 'ceded the province to the warlord Cao Cao in the same year'. Liu Qi, the elder son, had gone to Jiangxia in mid-208.

region.text: Jing Province under Liu Biao, 'covering present-day Hubei and Hunan'

ledger.note: 208: Liu Biao's domain ends. After Red Cliffs (winter 208/209) 'the commanderies in Jingzhou were thus split between the three contending warlords': Liu Bei took Nan, Lingling and Wuling, Sun Quan Jiangxia, Guiyang and Changsha, and Cao Cao kept Nanyang, Xiangyang and Nanxiang. The dissolve is dated to the surrender; the split follows in 209. [fx-36 H49, 1 Nov 2026: of the 209 split quoted above, only Jiangxia goes to Sun Quan here; the Liu Bei page has Liu Bei capture all four southern commanderies (Changsha, Lingling, Guiyang, Wuling), so Hunan goes to shu-han, and Changsha and Guiyang pass to Sun Quan at the 215 Xiang River partition (eastern-wu /ledger/7, shu-han /ledger/5).]

notes:
Liu Biao, Jing Province 190-208. 3 pages opened (Liu Biao, Jing Province, End of the Han dynasty). No Cliopatria row; the Han shape (ea-02-c) carries Jing until 207.
Unsettled: (1) Nanyang (south-west Henan) was one of Jing's seven commanderies but Wancheng was Zhang Xiu's 196-199 (End of the Han page: he surrendered Wancheng to Cao Cao in 197) and no page says whether Liu Biao held it: left out; (2) the Liu Biao page gives no year for the move to Xiangyang or the first seat; (3) the Huang Zu / Sun Quan fighting over Jiangxia is undated on the pages opened and not in the ledger; (4) the month 9 on 208 follows the page's footnote (8th month of Jian'an 13 = 29 Aug-27 Sep).
Counterparts: han-dynasty, cao-cao, eastern-wu, shu-han exist (ea-03 will write the last three); Sun Jian, Yuan Shu and Liu Bei have no dossier (Yuan Shu, south of the Huai from 191, is a candidate).
